In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the porcine granulosa cells and the oocyte itself are the source of the glycoconjugates which are incorporated into the ZP.
the ZP is a highly complex glycoprotein, which is synthesized by the oocyte and its surrounding cumulus cells.
the ZP of porcine oocytes contains a-mannose and b-Gal-(l-4)GluNAc residues, while b-Gal-(I-3)GaluNAc, a-fucose and sialic residues are not detectable in the ZP.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the oocyte, granulosa cells and ZP are the sites of synthesis and storage of the glucidic determinations present in the ZP.

the porcine oocyte and granulosacells contain a number of lectin-binding sites which are similar to those found in the zona pellucidacell surface, thus suggesting that both cell types are the site of ZP synthesis.
the ZP is a highly glycosylated structure containing several types of oligosaccharides.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ZP is not a homogeneous matrix but a highly heterogeneous structure with different lectin binding sites, suggesting that it could be a multivalent structure with different roles.
the ZP is a complex structure containing a large variety of glycoconjugates.
lectin binding is an important tool to investigate the composition of the ZP and the oocyte-granulosa cell interaction.
